title: Companies say AI is finally showing up in earnings
dek: Santander, Novartis and others reported early profit and revenue effects from AI as investors push for returns.
body:
Companies including Santander and Novartis told investors this quarter that artificial intelligence is beginning to affect the bottom line. Executives described AI-driven gains in revenue, cost reductions and improved profitability as shareholders press for concrete returns on AI investments.

## Why it matters

Public companies have spent billions on AI tools and projects over recent years. Investors have been watching for tangible financial payoffs rather than experimental projects or product demos. Reports from large, mainstream firms that AI is already moving the needle on revenue and costs signal a shift from investment to measurable financial impact — which could influence where capital flows next.

## The details

- Santander and Novartis are among the companies reporting that AI is starting to boost revenue, cut costs or improve profitability.
- Other companies made similar claims this earnings season, indicating a broader pattern rather than isolated cases.
- The announcements arrived as investors increasingly demand clear returns on the substantial AI spending companies have disclosed.
- The summary does not provide specific figures, timelines, or exact projects tied to the reported revenue or cost effects.
- It is not specified which AI technologies or vendors are responsible for the reported gains, nor how much of the companies’ results are attributable to AI versus other factors.

## What to watch

Look for next-quarter earnings and more granular disclosures that tie specific AI initiatives to revenue lines, cost categories or margins. Companies that can quantify AI’s contribution will likely face closer investor scrutiny and could influence competitors’ disclosure practices.

Source: [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/01/ai-investments-company-earnings.html)
author: Kelvane Club Desk
